episode.title: Percentage-of-context-window budgets scale the wrong way: ToolSearch preload never engages, and the always-on context warning never fires, on large windows
episode.before: At parent commit 6cfa25c967e348104609ee17ab020635c23f6ca0, ordinary deferred tools were hidden from the initial declaration list and exposed through the existing on-demand discovery path; GeminiClient.startChat warmed the registry, handled resume-history reveals, and then resolved the deferred-tool reminder without any context-window budget decision. There was no user setting or Config field for a deferred-tool preload threshold, and ToolRegistry had no operation that estimated the combined schema footprint and revealed the deferred set atomically. The parent already contained an always-on-context warning calculation based on contextWindowSize multiplied by a fixed ratio, and the pinned diff does not modify that warning path, so the warning symptom in the issue title is not evidenced as fixed by this episode.
episode.after: The implementation adds a session-start deferred-tool budget policy. The CLI exposes tools.toolSearch.threshold with default 10, forwards it into Config, and forces it to 0 in bare or safe mode. During startChat, after registry warm-up and resume reconciliation but before deferred-reminder construction, the client skips the budget path when the discovery surface is unavailable, the threshold is non-finite or non-positive, or the context window is invalid; otherwise it uses the configured context window or the model input-token-limit fallback, clamps a runtime threshold above 100 to 100, and passes a floored token budget to the registry. The registry considers every current deferred tool, including bundled and MCP tools, except always-loaded or explicitly visible tools, estimates the union as ceil(serialized-schema-characters divided by CHARS_PER_TOKEN), and reveals all candidates only when the union fits. If the union exceeds the budget, no candidate is newly revealed; already-revealed candidates still count toward the total. Revealed tools then appear in the initial declarations and are removed from the deferred reminder, while late registrations remain deferred until a later session start. The always-on-context warning code remains unchanged.
episode.diff: The pinned commit adds the threshold configuration contract and generated settings schema, a core Config getter/default, CLI-to-core propagation, a client-side context-percentage-to-token-budget gate, and a ToolRegistry all-or-nothing schema-footprint preload operation. It inserts the preload stage before deferred-reminder setup, adds debug diagnostics for no-candidate, over-budget, and preload branches, bounds the setting to 0-100 in the schema, adds a runtime upper clamp for hand-edited values, updates user/design documentation, and adds focused client, registry, and CLI tests. The commit changes 11 files with 516 insertions and 1 deletion. No implementation change touches the existing always-on-context warning calculation.

evidence_units.claim: The evidence bundle anchors issue 12029 to resolved commit 18cb393e4b59555d5e90f7003267fb69a43f6c77 with parent 6cfa25c967e348104609ee17ab020635c23f6ca0 and classifies the episode as bounded-resource-budget-control; issue body, comments, timeline, and linked pull-request metadata are unavailable.

The pinned commit is implementation-bearing and is titled `feat(core): preload deferred tools within a context-window threshold (#7922)`; its recorded parent is 6cfa25c967e348104609ee17ab020635c23f6ca0.

The pinned commit changes 11 files with 516 insertions and 1 deletion, including core client/config/tool-registry implementation, CLI configuration, generated settings schema, documentation, and focused tests.

The parent startChat implementation warmed the tool registry and processed resume-history reveals before resolving deferred reminders, but had no deferred-tool preload stage; the parent ToolRegistry exposed reveal/deferred-summary behavior but had no budgeted preload operation.
evidence_units.source: git show 6cfa25c967e348104609ee17ab020635c23f6ca0:packages/core/src/core/client.ts; git show 6cfa25c967e348104609ee17ab020635c23f6ca0:packages/core/src/tools/tool-registry.ts; parent-to-pinned diff for those files

evidence_units.claim: The checked-in design identifies the resource tradeoff: deferred-tool reveals rewrite the function-declaration prefix and invalidate prompt KV cache; it specifies a 10% context-window threshold, a union budget over bundled and MCP tools, all-or-nothing reveal, a zero opt-out, and session-start-only application.
Core ConfigParameters accepts a toolSearchThreshold percentage, Config stores it with a default of 10, and getToolSearchThreshold exposes the effective value to runtime consumers.
The CLI config assembly passes settings.tools.toolSearch.threshold into ConfigParameters and supplies 0 instead when bareMode or safeMode is active.
The settings schema defines the deferred-tool threshold as a number with default 10 and a JSON-schema minimum of 0 and maximum of 100; the generated VS Code schema mirrors type, bounds, and default.

The session-start budget adapter skips when ToolSearch is absent, the threshold is non-finite or non-positive, or the context window is invalid; otherwise it clamps the percentage to 100, selects configured contextWindowSize or tokenLimit(model,'input'), and passes floor(contextWindow*boundedPercent/100) to the registry.
The model input-token-limit helper returns a known model limit when available and otherwise falls back to DEFAULT_TOKEN_LIMIT, which is the fallback used by the client budget adapter.

startChat invokes the new deferred_tool_preload stage after tool_registry_warm and resume_deferred_tool_reveal but before deferred_reminder_setup; setTools subsequently obtains the declaration list from the resulting registry state.

The registry preload operation collects tools with shouldDefer while excluding alwaysLoad and visibleTools, sums JSON.stringify(tool.schema).length, converts the total with ceil(totalChars/CHARS_PER_TOKEN), leaves every candidate deferred when the union exceeds budget, and reveals every unrevealed candidate when it fits. Existing revealed candidates remain in the candidate set and therefore count toward the total.

The declaration path includes a deferred tool when it is not hidden; the hidden predicate requires shouldDefer, not alwaysLoad, not already revealed, and not listed in visibleTools. Therefore revealing a candidate makes its schema part of subsequent declarations, while always-loaded and visible tools do not need preload budget.

When ToolSearch is available, deferred-reminder setup filters out already-revealed tools; when ToolSearch is unavailable, the existing branch eagerly reveals all deferred summaries and returns no reminder. The new budget adapter intentionally returns before that existing eager-reveal branch when discovery is unavailable.

Client tests assert the default-token-limit fallback at a mocked 10% threshold, use of an explicit 50,000-token context window, no preload for threshold 0 or NaN, clamping a 200% threshold to a full-context budget, and no preload when ToolSearch is unavailable.

Registry tests assert that bundled and MCP deferred tools are all revealed when the union fits, none are revealed when it exceeds, bundled tools participate in the all-or-nothing union, already-revealed tools still count, and visible or always-loaded tools are excluded from the preload budget.
CLI config tests assert threshold forwarding at 25, defaulting to 10, and forcing 0 in safe and bare modes.

The parent and pinned versions use the same buildMemoryContextWarning logic: contextWindowSize is selected from configured/model/fallback sources, estimated tokens are compared with floor(contextWindowSize*MEMORY_CONTEXT_WARNING_RATIO), and the warning text is emitted above that threshold. The pinned diff adds threshold plumbing elsewhere but no hunk in this warning method.
evidence_units.source: packages/core/src/config/config.ts:3409-3434; git show 6cfa25c967e348104609ee17ab020635c23f6ca0:packages/core/src/config/config.ts around buildMemoryContextWarning; parent-to-pinned diff for packages/core/src/config/config.ts

The committed test files therefore remain direct validation oracles, but no green runtime result is claimed.

candidate_atomics.name: configure-deferred-preload-threshold
candidate_atomics.description: Expose a session-start deferred-tool preload percentage, carry it from user settings into core configuration, default it to 10, and disable the policy in CLI bare/safe modes.

semantic_action.intent: Make deferred-resource preloading an explicit, mode-aware session budget policy.
semantic_action.pre_state: No configuration value reaches core session startup to size deferred-tool preloading, so startup has no user-selectable percentage policy.
semantic_action.post_state: A threshold percentage is available to startup with default 10; ordinary CLI sessions receive the configured value, while bare and safe sessions receive 0.
semantic_action.validation: CLI tests assert configured forwarding at 25, default 10, and forced 0 in safe and bare modes; the settings schema supplies the declared numeric contract.

candidate_atomics.name: harden-threshold-domain
candidate_atomics.description: Defend the percentage invariant at both the declarative settings boundary and runtime so a hand-edited value above 100 cannot allocate a budget larger than the full context window.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent out-of-range percentage input from turning a bounded preload budget into an oversized or effectively unconditional preload.
semantic_action.pre_state: The new percentage policy can be bypassed by hand-editing or otherwise supplying a value above 100 after static schema validation; the derived budget would otherwise exceed the whole context window.
semantic_action.post_state: Declarative validation accepts only 0-100, and runtime input above 100 is clamped to 100 before token-budget calculation; non-finite and non-positive values still select the no-preload branch.
semantic_action.validation: The generated and source schemas declare minimum 0 and maximum 100, and the client test supplies 200 and asserts a full-context budget rather than a budget above the context window.

candidate_atomics.name: derive-session-context-budget
candidate_atomics.description: Convert an accepted positive threshold and available model capacity into a floored token budget at session start, using the configured context window or model-limit fallback and skipping unsupported branches.

semantic_action.intent: Translate a percentage resource policy into a concrete token budget before deferred-resource reconciliation.
semantic_action.pre_state: A threshold policy exists, but startup has not derived the number of schema tokens that may be declared up front; explicit context capacity may be absent.
semantic_action.post_state: When deferred discovery is available and the threshold and context are usable, the registry receives floor(contextWindow*boundedThreshold/100); otherwise the budgeted preload call is omitted.
semantic_action.validation: Client tests cover the model-limit fallback at 10%, an explicit 50,000-token context at 10%, threshold 0, non-finite threshold, over-100 input, and missing discovery surface.

candidate_atomics.name: atomically-preload-fitting-deferred-set
candidate_atomics.description: Estimate the complete eligible deferred-tool schema union and reveal every candidate only when the combined estimate fits the supplied budget; preserve full deferral on overflow.

semantic_action.intent: Avoid incremental declaration-list and prompt-prefix churn for a small deferred set while retaining on-demand discovery for a set that exceeds the budget.
semantic_action.pre_state: Deferred tool schemas are hidden behind discovery, and the registry has no combined footprint decision; bundled and MCP candidates may coexist with already-revealed, visible, or always-loaded tools.
semantic_action.post_state: The registry estimates the union of eligible deferred schemas as ceil(serialized-schema-characters/CHARS_PER_TOKEN) and reveals all eligible unrevealed candidates iff that estimate is within budget; otherwise no candidate is newly revealed. Visible and always-loaded tools are excluded, while already-revealed candidates still count.
semantic_action.validation: Registry tests cover fit, overflow, bundled-plus-MCP all-or-nothing behavior, already-revealed accounting, visible-tool exclusion, and always-loaded exclusion; declaration-path code shows that revealed schemas enter the function-declaration list.

candidate_atomics.name: synchronize-startup-declarations
candidate_atomics.description: Run the budgeted reveal after registry warm/resume handling and before deferred-reminder construction so the initial declaration list and reminder reflect the same revealed state without introducing a mid-session preload mutation.

semantic_action.intent: Apply the resource decision at the stable startup boundary so preloaded schemas are declared initially and are not later reintroduced as deferred reminders.
semantic_action.pre_state: Startup would resolve deferred reminders without a budget stage, so any preload decision would either be absent from initial declarations or require a later declaration-list change.
semantic_action.post_state: Preload runs after warm/resume reconciliation and before reminder setup; revealed tools are included in the initial declarations and filtered from the deferred reminder, while the existing no-discovery eager-reveal branch and late-registration deferral remain intact.
semantic_action.validation: The client startup call site establishes the stage ordering; reminder and declaration consumers show how revealed state is applied; client tests cover the preload stage and the no-discovery skip branch. No direct prompt-cache measurement is present.

candidate_workflows.name: bounded-startup-deferred-resource-preload
candidate_workflows.description: Establish a bounded percentage policy, harden its domain, derive a token budget from actual context capacity, atomically reveal the complete eligible deferred set only when it fits, and construct the initial declarations/reminder from the resulting state.

workflow_graph.goal: Bound the amount of deferred-resource schema declared up front by a percentage of available context while avoiding partial preload and preserving on-demand discovery when the union is too large.
workflow_graph.entry_state: The parent startup path hides ordinary deferred tools behind discovery without a context-scaled preload policy or combined schema-footprint gate.
workflow_graph.exit_state: For a valid positive policy and fitting current deferred set, all eligible deferred schemas are in the initial declaration list and absent from the deferred reminder; for over-budget, disabled, invalid, or unavailable branches, no invalid budgeted preload occurs and the existing deferral/eager-reveal behavior remains.
unresolved_or_deferred: The no-preload branches are runtime predicates, not separate implementation stages: discovery unavailable, threshold non-finite or <=0, invalid context, and an over-budget union preserve the existing non-preload behavior.
Tools registered after startup remain deferred until a later session start; the design explicitly avoids calling this policy from mid-session setTools synchronization.
The prompt KV-cache stability benefit is reasoned from declaration-list ordering and design comments but has no direct end-to-end cache-hit measurement in the pinned episode.
The always-on-context warning named in the issue title is outside this workflow because its parent/current implementation is unchanged.
